answer_text: Simply set, 'parallel' means running concurrently on distinct resources (CPUs), while 'distributed' means running across distinct computers, involving issues related to networks. Parallel computing using for instance is not distributed, while parallel computing with is often distributed. Being in a 'distributed but not parallel' setting would mean under-using resources so it is seldom encountered but it is conceptually possible.
